notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/cardfeedback.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/cardfeedback.md at 4a044e7 (“docs: publish 6 Coin fixes on jfs-components v0.1.78-c7d3348”, 19 October), the same blobs on main and docs-next. The guide's Sources note was checked on 19 October 2026 on the build it names (mirror v0.1.78-c7d3348, Biscuit's main at c7d3348, which fixed #286), and the evidence was re-tested on c7d3348 on 19 October (first checked 17 October on a116616), so items citing either carry 2026-10-19 and 0.1.78-c7d3348. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). GitHub's compare of v0.1.78-c7d3348 and v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (195 files, 3 commits, complete) touches no CardFeedback, Button, VStack, Title, design-tokens, resolver or icons file; the only utils file it touches is web-focus-trap.ts. Installed CardFeedback.tsx matches every guide and evidence sentence used here, read from source, not run, with token values through the package's own getVariableByName: the card's modes are AppearanceSystem positive, Context Nudge&Alert and Semantic Intent System, then its modes prop (lines 70–75); the panel has padding 12, radius 12, gap 8, minHeight 59, a column from the top left (77–93); panel and icon are rgb(219,240,217) / rgb(38,171,33) positive, rgb(255,227,214) / rgb(240,110,15) warning, rgb(255,224,222) / rgb(245,0,48) negative; AppearanceBrand changes only the title and body colours (Primary rgb(15,13,10) / rgb(30,26,20), Neutral rgb(13,13,15) / rgb(26,28,31), Secondary and Tertiary darker purple and navy bodies), never the panel, the icon or the buttons; with onPress the root is a Pressable with role button, hover opacity 0.92, pressed 0.8, a #0c0d10 focus ring on the web, and disabled gives 0.5 and ignores presses; without onPress it is a plain View, and disabled does nothing (95–137); Icon is a 20 px box drawing the registry icon in appearanceFeedback/cardFeedback/icon/color, or its children (147–170); Content is a full-width column, gap 8 (177–188); Title 14/17/500 and Body 12/16/400, plain Text that wraps (194–238); Action is a wrapping row, gap 4 (244–255); every part merges the card's modes with its own, and Icon, Content and Action give their children the part's modes under the child's own, so a Button's own modes win (9–21). A default Button in Action takes the status colour with a white label at 12/14 type, padding 12 × 4 (25 px). Contradicted by the installed build and left out: nothing. Out of date and not used: the Sources “Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78, built from Biscuit’s main at c7d3348” (the CardFeedback code is the same on dbe0e02). Not used as a rule: the Sources “The card doesn’t read the app’s theme, so Color Mode has to come through its modes.” It holds on dbe0e02 (CardFeedback never calls useTokens), but the building rules keep Color Mode off components, and dark mode belongs to the brand team, so it is neither a rule nor a gap; a VStack reads the app's modes and passes them to its children (VStack.tsx 63–64, 89–91). Not recorded: style and testID (the building rules keep style overrides off Coin components; the guide's 328 px maxWidth is the docs' hosting, as the evidence's Hosting says); Context and Semantic Intent on the card, Dark and AppearanceBrand examples, which the evidence's Limits say the guide doesn't show; Figma's 328 × 123 frame, its solid-circle icon and its Status variants, beyond the rule to pick a matching icon; the playground. Anatomy: the Panel is the root and always renders; Icon, Title, Body and Action are parts people compose as children (children is optional), so they are not always present, as in Attached's dismissal (agent-pack/README.md, Decisions); Content, which wraps Title, Body and Action, is not one of the guide's anatomy parts and is recorded as configuration. avoidWhen rests on the evidence's record of Biscuit's handwritten upstream CardFeedback.mdx (the mirror ships no mdx: CardFeedback/ holds only CardFeedback.tsx), as form.json's does; the guide's own copy names no other component. Toast and EmptyState have entries, so those rules carry useInstead; Popup is a package export with no entry in this pack, so that rule has none. Strength: the States sentence on onPress (“use it only when the card has no buttons inside”) is required with scope everywhere, since the evidence's Limits say never to put Buttons inside a pressable card and the mdx says not to set onPress when the card has Button children; the same sentence's naming clause is an accessibility recommendation. “AppearanceBrand only shifts the title and body colour slightly” is everywhere: on dbe0e02 it changes no other token. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every component), no style, and VStack's Slot gap M is dropped (no guide sentence says this content needs it; VStack's gap is 8 by default, 16 with M). AppearanceSystem negative is set on the failed-payment cards because the outcome failed (Configuration: red for something that failed); positive is the default, so the pressable card sets no modes. The quieter second action keeps the guide's own Button modes, Semantic Intent Brand, AppearanceBrand Neutral and Emphasis Low, because the guide says Emphasis alone doesn't quieten a button in the status colour. building.md's provisional “Two actions in one place” (Emphasis Medium on the other) doesn't work inside CardFeedback.Action: through the installed resolver, Emphasis Medium or Low under the card's Semantic Intent System gives the same red rgb(245,0,48) button with a white label as the leading one; the guide's three modes give a transparent rgba(235,235,237,0) button with rgb(36,38,43) text, and all three are needed (AppearanceBrand Neutral with Emphasis Low alone stays red). Title has an undocumented entry and takes title and subtitle; VStack and Button have entries. Copy is the guide's own (Pay Rahul Sharma, ₹1,250 from HDFC Bank, Payment failed, Your bank declined the payment. No money was taken., Try again, Change bank, Payment successful, ₹1,250 was sent to Rahul Sharma.); the pressable card's accessibilityLabel, “Payment successful. View receipt”, is the guide source's. The icons are the guide's (ic_error, ic_status_successful), all in the installed registry. Left out of examples (three at most): Message only, the warning card, the Configuration trio, the content example and the Do & Don'ts, which the rules cover. Gaps: the Sources note's stale Storybook (on 29 October the published index.json, last modified 17 October 2026, still lists the four stories and the docs page the guide names); and the evidence's token gap, Emphasis alone on a System button, which the evidence calls a token gap noted on #286's re-test, not CardFeedback's, and which still holds on dbe0e02 through the resolver. Sorting (batch 10, round 1): the cross-check raised no flags and noted two borderline items. The In context wiring sentence (“Try again runs the screen’s own retry through the button’s onPress.”) read as example narration in configuration; it is gone, and the In context example still carries it. The quieter-action rule drops the guide's “here”; it stays as a recommendation, since Emphasis alone fails on every button in the status colour through the installed resolver and the guide's modes are the only way it documents. Round 2 (the final entry): three flags said Icon, Title and Body should be always present, because the guide's anatomy calls only the buttons optional; dismissed in reviews/cardfeedback.json, since in this pack required means the package always renders the part (README, Decisions) and CardFeedback renders only the parts people compose, as Nudge's and Empty State's entries record and Attached's dismissal settles. The round-2 notes also call the onPress rule's required strength justified, and the avoidWhen items' “upstream Storybook docs” (Biscuit's mdx, not the published page) acceptable.

examples.purpose: A failed payment on the Pay screen, the guide's In context: a VStack column with the screen's Title and a negative Card Feedback (AppearanceSystem negative, because the payment failed; nothing else sets modes). Try again's onPress is a placeholder for the screen's own retry; when the retry goes through, the screen swaps the card for a positive one, since the card doesn't change itself or time out.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <Title title="Pay Rahul Sharma" subtitle="₹1,250 from HDFC Bank" />
  <CardFeedback modes={{ AppearanceSystem: 'negative' }}>
    <CardFeedback.Icon icon="ic_error" />
    <CardFeedback.Content>
      <CardFeedback.Title>Payment failed</CardFeedback.Title>
      <CardFeedback.Body>Your bank declined the payment. No money was taken.</CardFeedback.Body>
      <CardFeedback.Action>
        <Button label="Try again" onPress={() => {}} />
      </CardFeedback.Action>
    </CardFeedback.Content>
  </CardFeedback>
</VStack>

from.quote: Try again runs the screen’s own retry through the button’s onPress.

examples.purpose: Two actions, the guide's States: Try again leads at its defaults and takes the status colour; Change bank is the quieter second action. Emphasis alone doesn't quieten a button in the status colour, so Change bank sets the guide's own modes, Semantic Intent Brand, AppearanceBrand Neutral and Emphasis Low, which render it transparent with dark text. The handlers are placeholders for the screen's own wiring.

<CardFeedback modes={{ AppearanceSystem: 'negative' }}>

</CardFeedback>
